summary: The failure is an expired client mTLS certificate on payment-service: the cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal had notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z, exactly when bank_api_error_rate jumped to 100% and payment_success_rate collapsed from 99.41% to ~2.5%, with logs showing 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)' and mTLS handshake rejections (F9, F10, F11, F8). The green dashboard is an observability artifact: payment-service still accepts inbound HTTP and returns no 5xx, so its HTTP error-rate panel stayed flat at ~0.2% (F7), and the real failure is only visible on the bank-call path. The leading competing hypotheses are excluded by mechanism and timing: the only config change (cfg-2502, bank timeout 3000->5000 at 11:20Z) alters a timeout, not a credential, and precedes onset by ~55 min, while no change of any kind occurred near 12:15Z (F2, F13, F14, F16). Confidence is medium (0.60) as rated by the reviewed analysis; the residual uncertainty is that no PKI/cert-rotation record and no bank-side telemetry could be checked.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Expired client mTLS certificate on payment-service (credential expiry) breaks the bank-partner-api call path
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The client certificate that payment-service presents to bank-partner-api (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal) expired at exactly 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z. The bank rejects the handshake with 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)', so every bank call fails; payment-service accepts HTTP requests (no 5xx, so HTTP error-rate panel stays green) but marks transfers PENDING_RETRY, collapsing payment_success_rate to ~2.5%. The fault originates in payment-service's own client credential, not in the bank, not in a shared component, and not in any app deploy/config change.

causal_chain.claim: The mTLS client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal has notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z and no rotation happened (no cert-lifecycle change record exists).
Cert expiry at 12:15:00Z coincides with the exact start of the 12:15Z failure bucket; first concrete log is PENDING_RETRY at 12:15:27Z.

bank-partner-api rejects the presented cert with 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)' (171 occurrences, first 12:16:44Z); payment-service marks 140 payments PENDING_RETRY for mTLS handshake rejection.
bank_api_error_rate jumps 0.21% -> 100.0% at the 12:15Z bucket and stays 100%; payment_success_rate collapses 99.41% -> 2.45%.
The failing call is synchronous from the customer's perspective but returns success/202 to the caller, so HTTP 5xx error_rate stays flat at ~0.22% and the dashboard remains green.
Blast radius stays confined to the payment->bank-partner-api path; no shared-component or neighbor propagation signature appears.
No deploy or config change exists at or near onset (11:50Z-12:30Z: zero changes), so the removal of prior alternatives is consistent with a pure credential-time trigger.

assumptions: The cert that expired is the one actively presented for the bank call (rather than a stale/unused cert also appearing in logs).
The external bank did not independently start rejecting anything at the same time; the alert-45 signature is generated by the presented cert's validity window.

ranked_hypotheses.title: cfg-2502 (bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000) induced the transfer failures
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The only app config change in the entire window — payment-service bank.api.timeout_ms raised 3000->5000 at 11:20Z 'after partner advisory' — altered the bank-call path in payment-service and is responsible for the failures reported at 12:32Z.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2502 raised bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000 on payment-service at 11:20Z, the only change in the window.
Failures appeared within the same incident window, so the change is temporally the nearest candidate.

assumptions: A longer timeout could cause or expose handshake/transfer failures.
Bank-call failures would present as mTLS rejection.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Onset is pinned to exactly 12:15:00Z by the cert notAfter timestamp (F9/F11), ~55 min after cfg-2502 (F16), and the ~55 min quiet gap after the change weakens any causal link. Mechanistically, cfg-2502 changes a timeout value, not a cert, endpoint or handshake parameter, yet the error signature is a TLS expired-certificate alert (F10). No change of any kind exists in 11:50Z-12:30Z (F13). The trigger is a credential time-boundary, not this config.

ranked_hypotheses.title: External bank-partner-api degraded (dependency_failure), failing payment transfers
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The bank-partner-api / bank side degraded (matching precedent HIST-105 'Bank partner API returned 5xx'), causing payment-service bank calls to fail and transfers to remain incomplete while payment-service's own HTTP endpoints still returned success.

causal_chain.claim: bank-partner-api is an external dependency (has_telemetry=false) on the payment path.
Historical precedent HIST-105 describes a bank-partner-API failure causing payment-service payment failures.
Calls to bank-partner-api began failing at the 12:15Z bucket, collapsing payment_success_rate.
package of external failures would not show on the payment-service HTTP 5xx panel.

assumptions: The partner advisory behind cfg-2502 reflects real partner degradation (Gap: no partner telemetry at all).
The partner's rejection is not caused solely by the caller's expired certificate.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The actual error is generated on the client side: the specific expired cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal with notAfter exactly equal to the onset bucket (F11), and alert 45 'expired certificate' is a client-certificate validity outcome (F10). A partner-side degradation would not produce a client cert expiry perfectly aligned to the failure start second. HIST-105 is explicitly a lead, not evidence, and the partner has no telemetry to support it (F5, Gap).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared dependency (ledger-db or kafka) degraded by the 10:30Z settlement-service v1.9.0 deploy, propagating into payment-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: settlement-service v1.9.0 ('Batch settlement report export', 10:30Z, shared ledger-db and kafka) increased load or lock contention on a shared component, degrading the shared datastore/queue and causing payment-service transfer failures, with the fault originating in the neighbor service or the shared resource rather than in payment-service itself.

causal_chain.claim: settlement-service v1.9.0 deployed at 10:30Z, shares ledger-db and kafka with payment-service, and was not rolled back.
Shared ledger-db/kafka faults can propagate from a neighbor into payment-service.
payment-service's HTTP error-rate panel stayed green while customers reported transfer failures.
This produced PENDING_RETRY payments and a collapsed success rate from ~12:15Z onward.

assumptions: A shared-component degradation would surface as an mTLS handshake rejection against bank-partner-api.
settlement-service's batch export would affect ledger-db/kafka enough to break bank calls. (Gaps: shared-component metrics were never queried — budget ran out).
The ~105 min quiet gap between deploy and onset is incidental.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The failure signature is explicitly a TLS expired-certificate (alert 45) on the payment->bank-partner-api path (F10/F11), not a DB or queue error; payment-service's DB/queue branches were not the failing branch (F17). Blast radius is confined to the bank path with no shared-component or neighbor propagation signature, and settlement-service itself shows only benign GC/NTP warnings (F12). Onset at exactly 12:15:00Z is ~105 min after the deploy and ~105 min of silence post-deploy (F16), and zero changes existed near onset (F13). The only surviving temporal anchor is the cert notAfter.

facts.statement: payment-service's client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal has notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z, coinciding exactly with the start of the 12:15Z failure bucket; the remote bank returns 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)'.

Failure signatures in payment-service logs (12:00-13:59Z) are dominated by 'bank-partner-api call failed: remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45)' x171 (first 12:16:44Z) and 'payment <id> marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected' x140 (first 12:15:27Z); logs continue through the latest data at 13:58:39Z.

bank_api_error_rate on payment-service jumped from 0.21% at 12:10Z to exactly 100.0% in the 12:15Z bucket and stayed 100.0% through 13:55Z, while payment_success_rate collapsed from 99.41% (12:10Z) to 2.45% (12:15Z), averaging ~2.5% thereafter.

payment-service HTTP error_rate (HTTP 5xx) stayed normal across the whole incident window (0.23% at 12:00Z, 0.21% at 12:15Z, min 0.1 / mean 0.22 over 120 points), which is why the dashboard stayed green while transfers failed.
True onset is the 12:15Z 5-minute metric bucket (failures began between 12:10Z and 12:15Z), earlier than the report's ~12:17Z estimate.
In the tight window 11:50:00Z-12:30:00Z around onset there were zero deployments and zero config changes across all services.

Exactly one config change exists in 2026-04-01T00:00Z-2026-04-02T13:59Z: payment-service bank.api.timeout_ms raised 3000 -> 5000 at 11:20:00Z by p.nair ('Raise bank API timeout after partner advisory') — a timeout value on the bank call, not a cert, credential or endpoint change.

The only deploy in the wider 00:00Z-13:59Z window was settlement-service v1.9.0 at 10:30:00Z ('Batch settlement report export', live, not rolled back), a payments-org neighbor sharing ledger-db and kafka; it precedes onset by ~105 minutes.

Blast radius appears confined to the payment->bank-partner-api path: settlement-service shows only benign signals in the window (3 WARN total — 2 GC pauses, 1 NTP clock drift, none payment-related), and the failing branch is external bank-partner-api (has_telemetry=false) rather than the shared ledger-db or kafka branches.
bank-partner-api is external with no logs/metrics of its own, so the partner side must be observed through its callers.

assumptions: Assumption: the certificate that expired is the one actually presented on the live bank call, not a stale or unused cert that also appears in logs.

Assumption: the alert-45 'expired certificate' rejection is generated by the presented client certificate's validity window, and the external bank did not independently begin rejecting traffic at the same moment for another reason.

Assumption: no cert-rotation or PKI change is represented in the deployment/config change history, because those tools do not cover PKI lifecycle records — i.e. the causal 'change' (expiry) lives outside the observed change feeds.

Assumption: the 10:30Z settlement-service deploy and the 11:20Z cfg-2502 timeout change are unrelated to the failure, based on the ~105 min and ~55 min gaps and on the fact that neither touches the credential or handshake path.

Assumption: the 5-minute metric bucket resolution is accurate enough that the cert notAfter=12:15:00Z is effectively the onset instant, rather than the onset merely falling inside the 12:10-12:15Z interval for another reason.

recommended_actions.action: Immediate mitigation: renew/reissue the payment-service client mTLS certificate for CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal and deploy the new credential to payment-service (or confirm the replacement cert is already staged and reload it), then verify bank_api_error_rate returns to baseline and payment_success_rate recovers toward ~99%.
recommended_actions.rationale: The cert expired at 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z and bank_api_error_rate is pinned at 100.0% with 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)' — rotating the presented credential is the direct fix.

recommended_actions.action: Immediate: after rotation, drain/retry the backlog of payments marked PENDING_RETRY (140+ handshake-rejected transfers) and confirm they complete rather than accumulating.
recommended_actions.rationale: Transfers were marked PENDING_RETRY rather than failed, so they must be reattempted once the bank path works; queue/lag impact is unmeasured (data gap).

recommended_actions.action: Immediate (safe, discriminating): while mitigation is in progress, do NOT roll back settlement-service v1.9.0 and do NOT revert cfg-2502 as the first move; instead query shared-component metrics (ledger-db, kafka timeseries/depth) and payment-service latency_p99_ms to definitively exclude a shared-component or queue-side contribution.
recommended_actions.rationale: These are the untested branches; they are rejected by mechanism but were never measured, and a cheap read either closes the gap or overturns the conclusion. Neither deploy nor config is co-located with onset.

recommended_actions.action: Short term: instrument the bank-call path explicitly — alert on bank_api_error_rate and payment_success_rate (not just on HTTP 5xx error_rate) so credential/handshake failures cannot hide behind a green HTTP panel.
recommended_actions.rationale: The HTTP error_rate metric stayed flat at ~0.2% throughout because the failing path returns no 5xx; the real signal was bank_api_error_rate at 100%.

recommended_actions.action: Short term: add a pre-expiry certificate monitor/alert (e.g. warn at 30/14/7 days before notAfter) for payment-service's client certs and add an automated read of presented cert notAfter into the observability stack.
recommended_actions.rationale: The failure appeared within seconds of notAfter with no prior alerting; expiry was the entire trigger and no change coincided with onset.

recommended_actions.action: Long term: automate client-certificate rotation/renewal for the payment->bank-partner-api mTLS credential and record cert lifecycle events in a change feed, since change-history tools currently expose only app config and deploys.
recommended_actions.rationale: The one thing that changed at onset was the cert validity boundary, and the cert lifecycle was invisible to the change-history and PKI tooling queried (data gap).

recommended_actions.action: Long term: establish a synthetic bank-partner-api probe (caller-side health check that exercises the mTLS handshake end-to-end) since the partner has no telemetry of its own.
recommended_actions.rationale: bank-partner-api is external with has_telemetry=false; failures can only be observed indirectly via the caller, which caused the detection delay and left open whether the partner also changed anything.

data_gaps: No telemetry exists for bank-partner-api (has_telemetry=false); partner-side latency/error changes could not be checked and the partner advisory behind cfg-2502 could not be confirmed as real degradation.

Tool budget ran out before querying available_metrics/timeseries for shared components (ledger-db, kafka) and for api-gateway/settlement-service, so a shared-component signal at ~12:15Z could not be excluded by measurement.
Deployment history was only queried for 2026-04-02; earlier days were not checked, so a pre-midnight change is not fully excluded.
Kafka queue depth/lag and payment-service latency_p99_ms were never queried, so the async/queue-side blast radius and latency impact of the PENDING_RETRY backlog are unmeasured.
payment-worker and payment-queue are not valid service names (log queries failed not_found), so the worker/queue success-failure ratio could not be measured as a distinct service.
Metric buckets are 5 minutes, so onset is bounded to (12:10Z, 12:15Z] rather than an exact second.

No PKI/cert-rotation record was found for CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal; change-history tools expose only app config and deployments, so who owned the rotation and whether it was expected is unknown.
bank-partner-api log query failed (not_found), so the bank-side handshake rejection could not be corroborated from the partner's view.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Evidence that the cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal was not the credential actually presented on the failing bank calls (e.g. a different, still-valid cert in use) would break H1.

Observation of bank-partner-api-side degradation concurrent with onset (e.g. partner returning 5xx/alert 45 to callers with currently valid certificates) would shift support toward the dependency_failure hypothesis H4.
A shared-component signal at ~12:15Z — e.g. ledger-db saturation or kafka depth/lag spike aligning with onset — would reopen the bad-deployment/shared-dependency hypothesis H3.
Finding a config/endpoint/handshake change on the payment->bank path at ~12:15Z (rather than only the 11:20Z timeout change) would implicate H2 or a change-driven cause.

Confirmation that the handshake rejection is purely a local TLS-version or cipher mismatch rather than a cert validity failure (e.g. rejection despite a valid notAfter) would invalidate the credential-expiry mechanism.
Failure of payment_success_rate and bank_api_error_rate to recover after cert rotation would falsify H1 as the sole root cause.

findings.statement: No deployments occurred in the incident window 11:00Z-13:59Z across all services (count 0). The only deploy in the wider 00:00Z-13:59Z window was settlement-service v1.9.0 at 10:30:00Z ('Batch settlement report export', status live, not rolled back) -- a payments-org neighbor that shares ledger-db and kafka with payment-service.

Exactly one config change exists in 00:00Z-13:59Z: payment-service bank.api.timeout_ms raised 3000 -> 5000 at 2026-04-02T11:20:00Z by p.nair, described as 'Raise bank API timeout after partner advisory'. It affects payment-service itself and precedes the 12:32Z report.

payment-service dependency graph (edge = caller -> callee): api-gateway -> payment-service (http); payment-service -> ledger-db (db); payment-service -> bank-partner-api (external, has_telemetry=false); payment-service -> kafka (queue-produce). Shared components: ledger-db (postgres) and kafka, both marked shared=true; bank-partner-api is external with no telemetry.

ledger-db is a shared postgres used by four services: order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service; kafka is a shared queue used by order-service (produce), payment-service (produce), settlement-service (consume) and notification-service (consume). A fault in either shared component can therefore propagate to payment-service from a neighbor.

Historical precedent search returned no incident matching 'green dashboard but real payment failures'. Closest matches are dependency_failure precedents: HIST-105 (2025-11-19, 'Bank partner API returned 5xx for 40 minutes', payment-service payment failures) and HIST-103 (2025-10-21, external exchange API outage causing upstream timeouts); other matches were credential_expiry (HIST-106), bad_deployment/auth regression (HIST-109) and ledger-db resource_exhaustion (HIST-114). The tool notes these are 'leads, not evidence about the current incident'.

True onset is the 12:15Z metric bucket (5-min granularity, so failures began between 12:10Z and 12:15Z), earlier than the report's 12:17Z guess. The first concrete error log is a payment marked PENDING_RETRY at 12:15:27Z, and the explicit cert-expiry signature appears at 12:16:44Z.
